{{nihongo|'''Ashiinaba Shrine'''|葦稲葉神社}} is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|Q160734|qid=Q160734}}{{ill|Itano District, Tokushima|Q1156025|qid=Q1156025}}{{ill|Kamiita, Tokushima|Q1350072|qid=Q1350072}}. {{nihongo|'''Ashiinaba Shrine'''|葦稲葉神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Awa Province (Tokushima)]].

== Enshrined deities ==
'''Ashiinaba-no-Kami''' ({{ill|Ukanomitama|qid=Q3080728|lt=Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto}}) is enshrined as the principal deity, with '''Kagaehime-no-Mikoto''' ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kusanohime-no-Mikoto}}) {{ill|Co-Enshrinement|Q11412524|qid=Q11412524}}.

== History ==
Two main halls stand side by side; the western one (on the left when facing them) is Ashiinaba Shrine (the eastern one is the {{ill|Sessha|Q135009904|qid=Q135009904}} Tonomiya Shrine).

Although the date of foundation is unknown, the shrine has been worshipped since ancient times. In the {{ill|Rikkokushi|Q1151168|qid=Q1151168|lt=national histories}}, it is recorded that in the 9th year of {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|Q1075605|qid=Q1075605|lt=Jōwa}} ({{ill|842|Q24730|qid=Q24730}}), it was promoted from having no rank to Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade<ref>“{{ill|Shoku Nihon Kōki|Q1041301|qid=Q1041301}},” entry for the 2nd day of the 10th month, 9th year of Jōwa.</ref>. It was later promoted to Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade, and in the 9th year of {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} ({{ill|867|Q30347|qid=Q30347}}) it was further elevated from Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade to Senior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade<ref>“{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}},” entry for the 23rd day of the 4th month, 9th year of Jōgan.</ref>. In the 16th year of the same era it was promoted to Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade<ref>Same source, entry for the 14th day of the 3rd month, 16th year of Jōgan.</ref>, and in the 3rd year of {{ill|Gangyō|Q747451|qid=Q747451}} ({{ill|879|Q25001|qid=Q25001}}) to Junior Fourth Rank, Upper Grade<ref>Same source, entry for the 23rd day of the 6th month, 3rd year of Gangyō.</ref>. It is thus recognized as a {{ill|Kokushi genzaisha|Q118304363|qid=Q118304363}}.

The jointly enshrined Kagaehime-no-Mikoto is identified with the small shrine “Kagaehime Shrine” listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} for {{ill|Awa Province (Tokushima)|Q907457|qid=Q907457}}{{ill|Itano District, Tokushima|Q1156025|qid=Q1156025}}, and is regarded as a {{ill|Massha|Q135009906|qid=Q135009906}}<ref>There is also a theory that identifies it with a small shrine within the grounds of {{ill|Ōasahiko Shrine|Q723417|qid=Q723417}} in {{ill|Naruto, Tokushima|Q460812|qid=Q460812}}, Ōasa Town.</ref>. The time and circumstances under which it was enshrined together are completely unknown, but in this area stands the low yet beautifully shaped {{ill|Mount Ōyama|Q11434564|qid=Q11434564|lt=Mount Ōyama}}. As the shrine is located almost at the center of the {{ill|Alluvial fan|Q465088|qid=Q465088}} on its southern foothills, it is conjectured that the mountain itself was revered as a deity and that both deities were enshrined as {{ill|Guardian deities|Q131278957|qid=Q131278957}} of the rice fields spreading across the foothills<ref name="調査報告">Akiyama, “Kagaehime Shrine.”</ref>.

According to shrine tradition, in ancient times the shrine was located in a reed field called Ashinohara in Ōyamahata on the mid-slopes of Mount Ōyama<ref>Nearby is {{ill|Taisan-ji (Kamiita)|Q3514063|qid=Q3514063|lt=Ōyama-ji}}, said to have been founded in the {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}.</ref>. Due to flooding it was moved to Miyagadani, and later, after suffering arson, it was relocated to its present site on the southern foothills<ref name="調査報告"/>. However, a {{ill|Dōtaku|Q2312868|qid=Q2312868}} was also excavated near the present site in the 4th year of {{ill|Taishō era|Q329174|qid=Q329174}} ({{ill|1915|Q2084|qid=Q2084}}), suggesting that a large settlement had already developed in this area as early as the {{ill|Yayoi period|Q207858|qid=Q207858}}. Furthermore, numerous {{ill|Kofun|ca|Kofun|cs|Kofun|da|Kofun|de|Kofun|eo|Kofun|es|Kofun|fa|کوفون|fi|Kofun|fr|Kofun|he|קופון (רוגם)|hr|Kofun (grobnica)|it|Kofun|ja|古墳|ko|고훈|my|ခိုဖွန်း|pl|Kofun (kurhan)|pt|Kofun|ru|Кофун (захоронение)|simple|Kofun|th|โคฟุง|tr|Kofun|uk|Кофун|zh|古墳|qid=Q1141225}} are distributed around the foothills of Mount Ōyama, indicating that development progressed from the Yayoi period onward<ref name="調査報告"/>. During the {{ill|Meiji era|lt=Meiji period|qid=Q3125096}}, the shrine’s {{ill|Shakaku|ja|社格|ko|사격 (신토)|zh|社格|qid=Q10444029}} was that of a {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}.

== Subsidiary and branch shrines ==
* Tonomiya Shrine – Enshrines {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993}} and stands as a subsidiary shrine of the same scale immediately east of the main shrine’s main hall. The alternative name “Tonomiya” of this shrine refers to this.

In addition, there are several {{ill|Massha|Q135009906|qid=Q135009906}} nearby, including Shingū Shrine, Tsurugi Shrine, and Yamagami Shrine.
